correctness.rationale: Nonzero zero-divisors of A×F divide into blocks A=(0,u), B=(x∈m\{0},0), C=(x∈m\{0},u), E=(unit,0), of sizes s-1,h-1,(h-1)(s-1),h(q-1). For all pairs except two units-with-zero-second-component, nonzero square-zero m witnesses or the complementary idempotent give weak annihilator-product adjacency; E–E is not weak because both annihilators lie in the field factor. Subtracting the ordinary zero-product relation yields cliques A,C and only A–C, C–E, E–B interblock edges. Counts of vertices and edges follow, and a size h(s-1) clique with explicit proper coloring proves omega=chi; E plus one A proves alpha=h(q-1)+1. Graph substitution preserves perfectness. The twin-free quotient P4 and nontrivial internal-block reversal incompatibility recover a,b,c,d and hence q,h,s, but not the local ring. Separately enumerated annihilator witnesses for Z/4Z×F2 yielded the predicted 5-vertex 5-edge degree pattern [1,2,2,2,3]. The universally quantified statement follows from the ring/graph proof, not the finite example.
residual_risks: Requires one square-zero nonfield local factor and one field factor; no general finite-ring or higher-nilpotency theorem.

The theorem handles arbitrary nonprincipal square-zero ideals, not just sample chain rings.
